protections: Own-key copy into a destination object must not follow the inherited __proto__ accessor or recurse into Object.prototype: the deep merge/fill loops and the clone/mix copy loops must skip dangerous own keys before reading or writing the destination (src/object/deepMixIn.js:22-29, src/object/deepFillIn.js:15-22, src/lang/deepClone.js:20-22, src/object/mixIn.js:23-25, src/object/merge.js:22-28).
Dotted-path writers must not resolve inherited __proto__/constructor/prototype segments while creating the namespace they then assign into (src/object/namespace.js:8-14, src/object/set.js:7-12).
Dotted-path resolution used by readers and deleters must not walk through prototype objects on the traversed segments (src/object/get.js:8-16, src/object/has.js:8-10, src/object/unset.js:8-14).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: deepFillIn only writes a key when the current value is null/undefined, so a reader can argue the __proto__ slot is already non-null and can never be filled; the report's own route is the sibling deepMixIn, and the advisory history presents this function as the one already dealt with by the earlier fix.

set/namespace take the dotted path from the caller rather than from the untrusted object the report describes, and their documented job is just to create nested properties, so they do not look like merge input; a fix that only rejects the literal __proto__ segment also leaves the constructor.prototype form working.

unset writes no attacker-controlled value; it only deletes a property that already exists, and get/has are read-only, so this looks outside a pollution advisory; moreover the shared lower layer (get) must keep answering true for constructor/toString, which makes a blanket segment ban wrong.

these loops build a fresh object the caller owns: an own __proto__ key re-parents the returned clone or merge result, but Object.prototype itself is never written, so a global-pollution test on ({}) cannot observe it.

conflicts.what: The natural shared path validator for T3 must ban traversed constructor/prototype segments, but the must-keep-working behaviour of the T4 lower layer requires has(obj,'constructor') to stay true and get(foo,'bar.lorem.toString') to keep traversing (tests/spec/object/spec-has.js:32, tests/spec/object/spec-get.js:20-40); the write-path guard must therefore be stricter than the read-path guard.

The only shared choke point both deep-copy loops pass through is forOwn/forIn, but filtering __proto__ there also changes public enumeration (keys/values/size use forOwn, src/object/keys.js:6-12, src/object/values.js:6-11), so the two traps need their own copy-site guards.

fairness_risks: has(obj,'constructor') and has(obj,'toString') must remain true (tests/spec/object/spec-has.js:26-32, 59-65) while unset must not delete through those names; one blanket segment ban applied to read and write paths breaks this.
get() must keep traversing through functions and primitives (tests/spec/object/spec-get.js:20-40); a guard that stops at any inherited or non-object property breaks these cases.

namespace() must reuse existing own child objects (tests/spec/object/spec-namespace.js:21-35, 45-60) and set() must not replace an existing child (tests/spec/object/spec-set.js:15-26); a fix that always allocates a fresh object, or that refuses constructor/prototype names outright, breaks legitimate data keys.

deepMixIn/deepFillIn must still copy non-plain values (arrays, regexps, custom instances) by reference (tests/spec/object/spec-deepMixIn.js:79-95, tests/spec/object/spec-deepFillIn.js:74-86); a rule that drops whole keys whose values are objects is not acceptable.
merge() must not modify its inputs (tests/spec/object/spec-merge.js:5-18); a fix that deletes dangerous keys from source objects in place breaks this.

design.why: Four sites needing four different judgements: T2 is the reported merge route; T1 is the same deep-copy operation implemented a second time in a function that looks safe because it only fills null slots; T3 is a different API family (dotted-path writer) where a __proto__-only guard still leaves constructor.prototype open; T4 is the read/delete family whose natural shared guard collides with has(obj,'constructor')===true. The dismiss reasons are genuinely different (twin function, fill-only semantics, caller-supplied path, read-only/delete-only plus a coupled must-keep value), and no valid single guard closes more than one group: forOwn is the only shared pass-through for T1/T2 but filtering there changes public enumeration, and get is the shared pass-through for T4 only. T5 is left out of the design because its effect is confined to the returned clone.

unverified: The fix commits 3fecf1333e6d (A) and 17ffdc2a9641 (B) are not present in this worktree; HEAD 2189378 is at package.json:4 version 1.2.2 and no file under src/ contains any __proto__/dangerous-key guard, so both fixes are absent here. The mapping A=deepFillIn / B=deepMixIn is inferred from the twin-implementation pattern, not read from either patch; if the two advisories name the twins the other way round, T1 and T2 swap origins and tiers.
Neither advisory text is in the tree; the description of which route the later report names (origin advisory_route) is inferred.

The same fresh-object re-parenting shape exists in other key-indexed writers (src/object/pick.js:11, src/object/omit.js:12, src/object/map.js:11, src/object/filter.js:12, src/array/toLookup.js:16, src/function/memoize.js:28); they are folded into the T5 judgement rather than listed separately because none of them can write Object.prototype.
src/object/fillIn.js:9 is not recorded as a trap: its `obj[key] == null` gate makes the inherited __proto__ slot non-null, so the key is skipped.
